title: Security posture discovery with Nebula Therapeutics
summary: Initial security posture discovery focused on SOC 2 / ISO requirements, SSO/SAML and RBAC needs, audit logging and KMS key management for a potential Private deployment. Customer leaned toward Dedicated or Private due to PHI concerns and data residency; asked for SOC2 docs, network architecture review, and a pilot checklist.
action_items: Alex Rivera: Share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation (by 2026-07-23)
Priya Patel: Provide architecture diagram for Private VPC deployment and KMS integration notes (by 2026-07-26)
Rita Gomez: Send list of compliance questions and required evidence for legal review (by 2026-07-24)
next_steps: Schedule a follow-up deep dive with Nebula infra team to review VPC peering and KMS (proposed 2026-07-28)
Run a short benchmark on Dedicated instance for latency sensitive paths with sample workload
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Rivera: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, account exec on this one, with Priya our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:12] Daniel Park: Hey Alex, good, thanks. Rita and Samir are here as well.
[00:18] Rita Gomez: Hi, thanks for setting this up. We wanted to focus on security posture today, especially around PHI handling.
[00:28] Priya Patel: Great, we'll walk through SOC two / ISO, SSO and RBAC, audit logs, and our KMS integrations. Quick note: I might pronounce things weirdly, so jump in if I mangle acronyms.
[00:40] Samir Khan: Haha, fair. We've skimmed the public docs, but we need details for our compliance pack — also curious on net- work layout for Private deploy.
[00:52] Alex Rivera: Absolutely. Quick qualification: are you leaning Hosted first or do you need Dedicated/Private out of the gate because of PHI?
[01:05] Rita Gomez: We're conservative — likely Dedicated or Private. We have a requirement to keep data in our VPC and control KMS keys for certain workloads.
[01:15] Alex Rivera: Understood. Redwood Dedicated gives dedicated GPU pools with isolation; Redwood Private gives a private control plane and optional on-prem. Both can integrate with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering. Priya, do you want to add on KMS and key custody?
[01:30] Priya Patel: Sure — we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS and can do HSM-backed keys for higher assurance. For Private deployments, keys never leave customer control if you bring your own KMS. For Dedicated, we can arrange a BYOK flow. There are some implementation notes: wrap keys, rotation cadence, access logs to CloudTrail.
[01:50] Rita Gomez: When you say BYOK, is the key material hosted in our AWS account, or do you still see any plaintext?
[01:56] Priya Patel: No plaintext. We use envelope encryption; the service never gets unwrapped key material. We keep an audit trail — but we'll send the architecture diagram.
[02:08] Samir Khan: That architecture diagram would be helpful. Also need to know about network peering, port lists, and whether we can disable internet egress for model servers.
[02:18] Alex Rivera: Yes, for Private we support VPC peering and restrict egress. For Dedicated there's also options for private connectivity. We'll include the ports and required endpoints.
[02:28] Daniel Park: SOC2 — do you have a current Type II report and scope? Which trust services categories?
[02:36] Alex Rivera: We do; we'll share our SOC 2 Type II report. Our scope includes security and availability, and we can provide mapping to controls. Also we have ISO 27001 cert — we'll include the attestation.
[02:48] Rita Gomez: Are audit logs granular? We need per-user, per-token logs for access and model invocation history for e-discovery.
[02:58] Priya Patel: Yes — audit logs include token-level events, model selection, timestamps, and request metadata. For Private, logs can be pushed to customer SIEM via CloudWatch or a syslog endpoint. There might be slight mismatches in field names — sometimes the auto- transcript says KV cash instead of KV cache, sorry — but logs do include KV cache hits for debugging.
[03:20] Samir Khan: Good. Retention — can we set retention policies ourselves? We have different retention windows for PHI and non-PHI.
[03:28] Alex Rivera: You can configure retention and export logs to your storage for long-term retention. For hosted customers retention is configurable by plan, but for Dedicated/Private we can implement custom retention policies.
[03:38] Rita Gomez: How about SSO — we run Okta. We need SAML with SCIM provisioning and role sync into RBAC.
[03:46] Priya Patel: Supported — SAML 2.0, SCIM for provisioning, and you can map Okta groups to Redwood RBAC roles. We have granular roles (admin, developer, auditor) and can do custom roles for least privilege.
[03:58] Daniel Park: Is session recording or console access audited for admins?
[04:02] Priya Patel: Yes, admin console actions are logged and you can export those events. We also support MFA for admin accounts and SSO enforced with conditional access if your IdP supports it.
[04:14] Rita Gomez: Any gaps for HIPAA specifically?
[04:18] Alex Rivera: Not a legal opinion, but we support Business Associate Agreements and technical controls expected for HIPAA: encryption at rest/in transit, audit logs, access controls. Our legal team will go through the BAA draft if you want.
[04:30] Samir Khan: Can we run a canary test — send synthetic PHI to see how the system behaves and validate logs and retention?
[04:36] Priya Patel: Yes, that is common. For Dedicated we can provision a small pool and run latency sensitive workloads. We can also show model fallbacks and routing policy behavior under load.
[04:48] Daniel Park: On- prem — we might need an air-gapped option for a small subset of models. Is that available?
[04:54] Alex Rivera: We offer an on-prem package for highly regulated workloads, but it involves more ops and licensing. We'll have to align on which models and quantization we support on-prem.
[05:06] Rita Gomez: Encryption in transit — TLS 1.2/1.3? Mutual TLS for internal service-to-service?
[05:12] Priya Patel: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported. Mutual TLS can be configured for inter-service communication in Private deployments. We'll include a network hardening checklist.
[05:24] Samir Khan: What about RBAC for model access — can we prevent certain teams from invoking certain models?
[05:30] Priya Patel: Yes, per-route and per- model permissions are supported. You can create policies that restrict model invocation to roles or service tokens. Also token scoping helps limit access per app.
[05:42] Daniel Park: Do you have an attestation of background checks or employee access controls?
[05:46] Alex Rivera: We have internal controls documented, and SOC covers personnel controls to an extent. For Dedicated where customer data is isolated, access is even more restricted; for Private it's fully under customer control.
[05:58] Rita Gomez: We need to verify logging retention meets our e-discovery SLA of 7 years for certain records. Can you support export to long-term cold storage?
[06:06] Priya Patel: Yes — logs can be exported to S3 Glacier or your archival storage. We'll include the export playbook.
[06:16] Daniel Park: How do rollouts and canary deploys affect auditability? If a canary fails and falls back to a different model, is that recorded?
[06:24] Priya Patel: Yes — rollouts are traceable. We log routing decisions, model variant used, fallback events, and latency/cost metrics. That data can feed into your monitoring.
[06:36] Alex Rivera: Wondering about pricing for Dedicated vs Private — but we'll send a pricing sheet separately. Today we want to confirm compliance fit.
[06:44] Rita Gomez: One more on KMS: can we rotate keys without downtime?
[06:48] Priya Patel: Yes, rotation occurs using key versions and envelope keys; it is designed to be seamless. We'll share the rotation flow details.
[06:58] Samir Khan: Any known limitations with quantized models and private HSM? I recall some vendors had issues with certain kernels.
[07:06] Priya Patel: We do kernel selection and quantization-aware runtime. On-prem deployments require validated quantization profiles; we'll include the supported matrix.
[07:18] Daniel Park: Great. Could you pull together a short compliance pack and timeline for a pilot? We need to present to legal on Friday.
[07:26] Alex Rivera: Yes — action items: we'll send SOC2/ISO, architecture diagram, pilot checklist, and proposed dates. Priya will own the infra deep dive.
[07:36] Rita Gomez: Also please include a sample contract excerpt for BAA and data residency clauses.
[07:42] Alex Rivera: Noted.
[07:44] Daniel Park: Any questions from your side?
[07:46] Priya Patel: Just to confirm — you want Private for PHI-critical flows and maybe Dedicated for others?
[07:52] Rita Gomez: Correct. We'll scope which endpoints need the highest isolation.
[07:56] Alex Rivera: Perfect. We'll follow up with docs and schedule the infra deep dive.
[08:02] Daniel Park: Thanks everyone.
[08:05] Rita Gomez: Thanks.
[08:07] Alex Rivera: Thanks, bye.

Notes: Transcript has occasional transcription noise (e.g., Speaker 2 labels, mis-heard acronyms). References to artifacts: \"SOC2 report (link)\" and \"Private VPC architecture diagram (link)\" to be attached in follow-up email. Recap and next steps agreed; action items assigned as above.
